request.deadline: 18-month funding period with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity and publish technical transition architecture, migration plan, and public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under published rules in Q4 2026.
Serve all public API traffic from the new stack and legally transfer Blockfrost IP to the governing entity in Q1 2027.
Open public consultation and publish a long-term sustainability proposal in Q2-Q3 2027.
Operate the public API with at least 99% monthly uptime and publish quarterly technical and budget reports during 2027.
request.recipient: Input Output Global / Input Output, with administration involving Intersect and CDH according to the document
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Blockfrost's transition into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public good and support 18 months of transition and operations.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is presented as a hosted REST interface that lets Cardano developers read from and interact with the blockchain without running their own node.
The proposal states that Blockfrost was founded in 2020 by Five Binaries and joined IOG in 2024 with the goal of decentralizing it.
The document cites Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey links showing Blockfrost hosted-platform usage rising from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal states that in the prior month Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The document states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the decentralized Blockfrost operator effort.
The proposal commits to transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets into a community-governed not-for-profit entity.

The proposed governance model includes a five-seat board, four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, with elections hoped for by year-end and appointment no later than Q1 2027.
The total requested budget is 9,832,979 ADA, stated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, with 79.1% for staffing, 19.3% for operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% for legal and accounting.

The proposal states that infrastructure costs and usage will be made public through a dashboard and quarterly reports, and that unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to move Blockfrost into community-governed not-for-profit stewardship, operate it for 18 months, transfer IP, establish governance, maintain public API service, and publish usage and budget reporting.
